selection: One previously unused open issue per distinct repository and owner, with a recorded issue age of at least 30 days and at least two non-bot participants; source commit and one relevant source file pinned. These are purposively selected, not a random production population.
design: Use three fresh ephemeral Codex processes per arm in paired randomized order with the same pinned source and issue archive; treatment adds a new Memex L3 store and its standard project manual. Earlier and later captured comments are revealed across sessions. The scoped deliverable is a source-grounded investigation and test/repair proposal, with a patch only when the assigned environment permits it. This is an investigator-defined shadow investigation, not an upstream request to these agents or an online production session.

primaryRubric.score: 0 materially wrong or no relevant work; 1 partial, uncertain or incomplete; 2 evidence-supported response meeting task-specific criteria; null insufficient evidence or missing review.
primaryRubric.review: Anonymous arm labels with retained original reviews; adjudicate valid score disagreements. Do not infer current behavior from historical reports alone.

limitations: Not 30 completed or independently verified outcomes.
The issue body is its present captured text, not necessarily its original unedited form; source snapshots are current relative to capture, not historical snapshots of early comments.
Some discussions contain public proposed fixes or later conflicting reports; one issue per repository does not prove statistical independence.
A pinned source file and acceptance rubric do not establish that each project’s dependencies, sandbox verifier or full test suite are ready.
AI reviewers share a gateway and are not independent human assessors; live-service, device and production costs can remain unknown.
blinding: Future arm assignments and random seed are retained privately until the respective experiments have concluded.
